paper.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning
paper.abstract: Multimodal large language models can write code and interpret rendered images of 3D designs, but it remains unclear whether they can produce executable parametric 3D programs that are geometrically precise, semantically aligned and assembly-consistent. We introduce P3D-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates this ability under a unified protocol across three task families: text-conditioned part synthesis, image-conditioned multi-part reconstruction and image-plus-annotation assembly composition, with metrics that jointly probe executability, geometric fidelity, topology, text-grounded constraints, multiview semantic alignment and part-level assembly structure. Evaluating frontier MLLMs and text-only LLMs, with CAD-specialized baselines included as reference points, on 400 text cases, 400 image cases and 203 annotated assemblies yields three findings. First, text-conditioned part synthesis exposes a gap between executable generation and parametric correctness, as explicit parameters do not reliably form coherent geometry. Second, on image-conditioned reconstruction the multiview Judge shows semantic recognition outpacing geometric alignment: the strongest MLLM scores J-sem = 8.2 versus J-geo = 3.2 out of 10, naming the object and its parts without recovering the dimensions needed for editable parametric output. Third, annotated assembly remains the hardest setting: long part-level and assembly-level annotations widen model differences, with weaker MLLMs dropping sharply in executable validity and structural consistency; even the strongest model reaches only 0.525 cross-format PartMatchF1, showing that explicit part recovery remains limited. Together these results expose a persistent gap between executable or visually plausible 3D programs and editable parametric designs with correct parameter dimensions and part relations.

The lower body is a single solid rounded base, and the visible upper geometry is made from three added solid sections rather than surface markings. The added material forms stacked circular and arc-shaped pads with nested depths, including a broader shallow tier and a deeper contained round continuation. Several inner loops create actual voids: small round openings and slot-like elongated openings pass through their respective raised sections. The curved outlines and cutaway arcs should remain rounded, and the bounding span of the separate circular features should not be interpreted as a rectangular plate.
